blocking.title: filesystem_confinement is bound into the signed attestation but never applied to the spawned worker
blocking.detail: run_confined_attested constructs the WorkspaceObserver and immediately drops it. spawn_confined receives no workspace root, no chroot/mount-namespace, no seccomp, and does not even set current_dir(workspace): the worker runs with the ambient filesystem view of its uid. The whole fs_policy/WorkspaceObserver machinery is exercised only in unit tests and never mediates the real process, yet filesystem_confinement is emitted in effectiveControls with requestedProfileDigest == effectiveProfileDigest — which the design defines as honoured without degradation. Journey 2 states the path sets are applied and 'attesting what was not enforced' is an explicit non-goal. An offline operator is told the marquee control was enforced when it was not: the worker can read every world-readable path and write anywhere its uid permits, outside the attested policy. No adversarial test asserts that a real spawned worker leaving the workspace is blocked — because it is not.

blocking.title: Process-group kill and process/resource limits are attested but not enforced; a worker's children survive the duration bound
blocking.detail: On timeout and on output flood only child.kill() is issued — SIGKILL to the direct PID. No setsid()/new process group and no killpg, despite process.killProcessGroup: true. Because the worker's stdio are its fd 0/1 on the private socketpair, any grandchild inherits the output fd AND survives the kill: it runs past maxDurationSeconds and holds the transport open. maxProcesses (fork-bomb bound) is never applied — setpriv is passed no rlimit and ProfileWire drops the field. Yet resource_limits is bound in effectiveControls and the full profile is bound as effective == requested. This is both a live confinement escape and an over-attestation with no mechanism behind it.

major.title: Worker identity drop is incomplete: gid unchanged, ambient capabilities not dropped, while process_isolation is attested
major.detail: The wrapper is `setpriv --no-new-privs --reuid <uid> --clear-groups`. There is no --regid, so the worker keeps the invoker's primary gid; the CI e2e runs as root, so the worker executes with gid 0 and --clear-groups removes only supplementary groups. Group-0-readable/writable files remain reachable. dropAmbientCapabilities is declared but setpriv is given no --ambient-caps/--inh-caps/--bounding-set. process_isolation and dedicatedIdentity are attested as effective while the identity transition is partial.

major.title: The profile's process and transport security block is inert — bound by digest as effective but never consumed
major.detail: ProfileWire deserializes only process.max_duration_seconds; dedicatedIdentity, denyPrivilegeEscalation, dropAmbientCapabilities, killProcessGroup, maxProcesses and the whole workerTransport block are parsed away, so nothing can enforce them. Combined with effectiveProfileDigest == requestedProfileDigest and coarse capability-name granularity, this is exactly the silently degraded confinement the design claims impossible by construction — it is possible here for every process/transport field except the duration.

minor.title: Capability guard is a substring scan with evadable matching
minor.detail: The guard enforces via source.includes(...). Rust paths are whitespace-insensitive, so `use std :: env ;` evades the std::env entry, and parent-module aliasing slips past module-prefix entries. Real enforcement is compensating (forbid(unsafe_code), the closed dependency allowlist, cargo fmt --check normalising whitespace), but the guard is described as the mechanical boundary, so its evadability should be acknowledged or fixed with token-aware matching.

minor.title: CI privileged e2e weakens sudo and runs the full toolchain as root
minor.detail: The step runs `sudo --preserve-env=PATH,... cargo test`, compiling the crate and its dependencies (build scripts, proc-macros) and running the test binary as root; --preserve-env=PATH defeats sudo's secure_path, a PATH-substitution escalation vector on shared runners. Prefer building unprivileged and running only the prebuilt test binary under sudo, with an absolute cargo path.

nonBlocking.title: The fail-closed output scan is a stub in the integration path
nonBlocking.detail: run_confined_attested hardcodes admit_scan(OutputScan::Complete): OutputScanIncomplete can never fire end to end, and no content inspection occurs before output leaves the boundary. Journey 4 is plumbed but not substantively realised at this stage.

nonBlocking.title: Attestation binds the worker binary digest but not the invocation; networkMode wording is stronger than what is enforced
nonBlocking.detail: sha256(program) is bound but not args or payload, so an operator cannot see how the worker was invoked. networkMode 'none' records that the harness opened no network; it does not mean worker egress was prevented (no namespace, no seccomp). ADR-0018 D2 documents network as closed-at-stage, so this is a deferral, but the attested value reads as a guarantee it does not provide.

nonBlocking.title: Positive controls confirmed
nonBlocking.detail: All 13 refusal codes have adversarial tests. base64url decode is strict with a re-encode round trip. Ed25519 verify recomputes the digest and rejects tampered content, wrong key and flipped signatures; the signed message carries schema-version domain separation. No unsafe (crate-level forbid). Dependency surface is a closed allowlist. The socketpair ends carry CLOEXEC, so the harness ends do not leak to the child. The signing seed is a caller parameter; no key material is logged or persisted. env_clear is verified to strip the host environment.

residualRisks: The pure layers (digesting, canonical policy, attestation assembly and verification) are strong and well tested; the defects are concentrated in the host/run wiring, where the attestation binds capabilities the confined spawn does not apply. The signed attestation is therefore not a faithful record of enforcement, which is this system's core promise.

Under the CI bootstrap the only containment actually applied is: dropped uid (not gid), no-new-privs, cleared supplementary groups, cleared environment, private socketpair stdio, output byte cap, best-effort direct-child duration kill.

ADR-0018 D2 network/secret closure holds for the harness's own code, but nothing prevents the confined worker from performing network egress; documented as deferred, yet the attested networkMode could be misread as egress prevention.

All findings are fixable within this crate: wire the observer mediation (or a real fs sandbox) into the spawn, add setsid+killpg, RLIMIT_NPROC, --regid and capability drops, parse the full process block, and either enforce or stop attesting the inert controls.
